wave: SECURITY / SEMANTIC PRESERVATION -- two independent id computations over the same ADL-authored free-text fields (DeclaredEdge.from/relation/to, BindingDecl.consumer/capability/provider) joined them with a bare, unescaped `:` delimiter: core::graph::engineering_graph's DeclaredEdge/Binding graph-projection arms, and runtime::census::build_census's fact_id computation for the same declarations. Both sit directly adjacent, in the same match statement or the same loop nest, to sibling code that ALREADY escapes this identical field set for this identical reason (core::language::adl::mod's own DeclaredEdge.id, and engineering_graph's ConstraintResult|Diagnostic arm) -- these two call sites were simply never given the same treatment.
wave_title: Twenty-second generation this cycle. After generations 20-21 closed the unescaped-delimiter-join bug class across every core::semantic identity_key(), delegated a background Explore survey to look for the same pattern in adjacent, not-yet-audited territory: core::graph::engineering_graph's earlier (pre-line-520) code and runtime::census::build_census's core fact-building loops. It found two real instances of the identical bug class, both directly beside already-fixed sibling code using the exact same fields.
priority_classification: security / semantic preservation -- live defects, independently confirmed by constructing concrete collisions and running them against the real, unfixed code before any change. Reachable from ordinary ADL authoring: ADL's relation/binding syntax is extracted by `parse_relation`'s simple `split_once("->")`/`split_once('=')`, with no charset restriction on the resulting from/relation/to or consumer/capability/provider text -- a relation or capability name containing a literal `:` (which ADL's own grammar does not forbid) is enough to trigger a collision.
gap_discovered_by: Delegated Explore subagent survey, explicitly scoped to (1) core/src/graph/engineering_graph.rs's first ~520 lines (before the SemanticObservation match already audited generations 20-21) and (2) runtime/src/census/mod.rs's build_census function and helpers (excluding the already-fixed dedup comparators). Both findings were independently re-verified before acting: read the real, unfixed DeclaredEdge/Binding arms in engineering_graph.rs directly, read the real, unfixed fact_id call sites in census/mod.rs directly, read core::language::adl::mod's own DeclaredEdge.id computation to confirm the established escaping precedent for this exact field set, and independently constructed and ran concrete collisions against the real unfixed code before writing any fix -- correcting one of the survey's own draft collision pairs in the process (its first attempt at a Binding collision held `provider` fixed and varied `consumer`/`capability` around the wrong join order; re-derived the correct crafted pair directly from the real `format!("binding:{}:{}:{}", consumer, capability, provider)` call).
key_finding:
Two independent, confirmed collisions:
1. `core::graph::engineering_graph`'s `SemanticFactKind::DeclaredEdge` arm (edge id) and `SemanticFactKind::Binding` arm (binding id and BINDS_TO edge id) joined `fact.subject`/`fact.predicate`/`fact.object` with a bare `:`, no escaping -- confirmed two genuinely different declared edges/bindings collapse onto one edge/binding id via a hand-constructed pair, run against the real unfixed code first.
2. `runtime::census::build_census`'s `fact_id` computation for `DeclaredEdge`/`Binding` facts (the census-layer projection that produces the very facts consumed by (1)) has the identical defect one layer upstream: `edge.from/.relation/.to` and `binding.consumer/.capability/.provider` joined unescaped into `fact_id`'s seed -- confirmed with the same technique, against the real unfixed code.
Both are the SAME root field class core::language::adl::mod's own `DeclaredEdge.id` already escapes (its own comment: "any of the three can contain a literal `:`... escaped before joining to keep two genuinely different relations from ever computing the same edge id") -- this generation extends that same fix to the two other, independent id computations over the identical fields that were never given it.
verification_before_acting: Read core::graph::engineering_graph.rs's real DeclaredEdge/Binding arms directly (lines 322-366), confirming the unescaped `:` join, and confirmed the immediately adjacent ConstraintResult|Diagnostic arm already escapes the identical field class for the identical reason -- a direct, in-file precedent for the correct fix.

Read runtime::census::mod.rs's real fact_id call sites for DeclaredEdge/Binding directly (lines 260-296), confirming the unescaped `:` join and that `fact_id` is a bare `stable_id("semantic-fact", seed)` with no escaping applied anywhere in the file (confirmed via grep).

Read core::language::adl::mod.rs's own DeclaredEdge.id computation directly, confirming it already escapes from/relation/to for this exact reason -- the established precedent this generation's fix mirrors.

Independently constructed a concrete collision pair for each of the three distinct join shapes (DeclaredEdge's 3-field join, Binding's 3-field id join with `capability` in the middle position, and Binding's separate 2-field BINDS_TO-edge join with a fixed literal in between) and ran each against the real, unfixed code before applying any fix -- correcting my own first attempt at the Binding collision after re-deriving the actual field order from the real source rather than assuming it matched DeclaredEdge's shape.

Re-ran this repository's own real self-census (cargo run -p atlas-cli -- systemize --root .) after all fixes, confirming coding_admission.blockers is still empty -- no behavioral regression on real, non-adversarial source.

design_decisions.question: Fix both files, or just one?
design_decisions.decision: Both. They are independent id computations over the same underlying ADL fields at two different layers (runtime::census::build_census produces the SemanticFact.id that later reaches core::graph::engineering_graph's DeclaredEdge/Binding arms, which then computes its OWN separate edge/binding id from the same subject/predicate/object text) -- fixing only one leaves the other's id computation still collision-prone, even though the fact.id computed by census/mod.rs and the edge/binding id computed by engineering_graph.rs are used for different purposes (fact identity vs. graph node/edge identity) and neither derives from the other.

design_decisions.question: Escape at the `fact.subject/predicate/object` level in engineering_graph.rs, or fix it further upstream only?
design_decisions.decision: Escape at both points independently, matching how the codebase's OTHER already-fixed instance (ConstraintResult|Diagnostic) is structured: engineering_graph.rs's SemanticFact consumer has no way to know whether the fact.subject/predicate/object it receives came from an already-escaped source, so it must defensively escape at its own join point too, exactly like the Diagnostic arm already does 12 lines below the DeclaredEdge/Binding arms it sits beside.
